I will keep to the wheat-maize rotation that fits Quzhou County best, because that is the cropping pattern I know, it matches our climate and irrigation conditions, and at my age I want a steady, familiar plan instead of taking on extra risk. I will put all my land into winter wheat first and then follow with summer maize on the same fields. I will use improved or hybrid seed rather than old saved seed, because I care more about stable yield, lodging resistance, and simpler field management than saving a small amount on seed. For wheat, I will manage fertilizer more steadily and irrigate several times if water is available, especially around key stages, because wheat here responds well to water and nitrogen. After wheat harvest, I will move quickly into summer maize so I do not lose soil moisture or sowing time. For maize, I will keep fertilizer balanced, use fewer irrigations than wheat if rainfall helps, and control weeds and insects with a limited number of pesticide sprays. I will use rotary tillage because it is easier, faster, and lighter work for me than deep ploughing, and it fits the machinery and habits I would rely on.
